quizzes.stem: A report on AI in the creative industries covers only visual arts, with nothing on music, writing or film. Every subagent finished its task, and the log shows three subtasks: digital art, graphic design and photography. Which change fixes the cause?

options.a: Loosen the relevance filter of the analysis agent so that fewer documents are dropped
options.b: Instruct the synthesis agent to look for missing coverage in everything it receives
options.c: Widen the queries of the search agent so that it returns more kinds of source
options.d: Check the coordinator's plan against the question's scopes, ahead of any delegation

explanation.d: The subagents did what they were assigned, so the plan is what to check, and it can be checked against the question.
explanation.b: Ruled out because it is a late substitute: "A downstream agent that is asked to notice gaps is a late and unreliable substitute for a check that costs one comparison."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the search agent worked within its scope: "each agent worked correctly within its scope, so widening it does not reach the scope that was never assigned".
explanation.a: is ruled out for the same reason: "the subagents did what they were assigned, and the fault is the assignment".

quizzes.stem: A run ends with a report marked complete. The film search timed out, nobody retried it, and the report holds nothing on film. Where is the defect?

options.a: The status is not derived from the scopes that were covered
options.b: The report agent should have written a longer summary of the other scopes
options.c: The search agent should have returned an empty list instead of an error
options.d: The timeout was set too short, so the search never had time to finish

explanation.a: A status must come from coverage.
explanation.b: Ruled out because more prose does not repair the claim: "A run is complete when every scope is covered."
explanation.c: Ruled out because an empty success hides the gap: "A failure with no context, or a failure turned into a success".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the defect is in what the report claims and not in how long the search waited: "It is partial otherwise, whatever the reason, and the report says which scopes are missing and why."

quizzes.stem: In the example, the film search times out, the alternative query is down as well, and the run goes on. What does the report carry?

options.a: Partial, with a note that names only the first query that failed
options.b: Complete, since the alternative query was tried before the scope was given up
options.c: Partial, with three of four scopes covered and a note that names both failed queries
options.d: Failed, with no report at all because one scope has no findings

explanation.c: The page says what the second run shows: "In that second run the status is `partial`, three of four scopes are covered, and the note names the two queries that failed."
explanation.b: Ruled out because trying is not covering: "A run is complete when every scope is covered."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the note names both: "the note names the two queries that failed".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the report still has value: "A report that did not cover film is still a useful report".

quizzes.stem: Under the module's bounded policy for failures, a search subagent times out and its error offers an alternative query. What should the coordinator do?

options.a: Retry the same query until it succeeds, however many attempts that takes in total
options.b: Retry with the suggested substitute once, then report the scope as not covered
options.c: Stop the whole run and return the error to the caller, who will decide
options.d: Mark the scope as covered and let the synthesis agent fill the gap

explanation.b: One retry through the alternative, then an honest gap.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the retry is bounded: "The coordinator retries once through an alternative and then stops."
explanation.c: Ruled out because one failed scope does not end the run: "A failure of one subagent does not end the run: the other scopes are still worth reporting."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a scope without findings is not covered: "A scope that is marked covered without findings is a claim that nothing supports."

quizzes.stem: Two publications report 12 and 14 for the same statistic, a year apart. How should the report treat them?

options.a: Report the value that more of the other documents seem to support, whichever it is
options.b: Report the newer value alone, since a more recent figure replaces an older one
options.c: Report the average of the two figures, since each is probably close to the truth
options.d: Show both values with their sources and dates, and give neither as the answer

explanation.d: A conflict is shown with both values, both sources and both dates.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the newer value is not picked in silence: "A conflict is two different values for one claim, not two sources for the same value".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the values are not blended: "the report does not average them and does not pick the newer one in silence".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the date is often the explanation: "a figure measured in one year and a figure measured in the next can both be right".

quizzes.stem: A search failed after it had already returned two usable results for its topic. How should the report record that topic?

options.a: As covered, because some usable results were returned for it
options.b: As uncovered, keeping what arrived but marking it incomplete
options.c: As covered once the synthesis agent has accepted the results
options.d: As missing, with the two results dropped so that they cannot mislead

explanation.b: Partial findings are kept and flagged, and the topic is still a gap.
explanation.a: Ruled out because partial is not coverage: "A partial result is information, and it is not coverage".
explanation.c: Ruled out because acceptance is not the test: "coverage is a property of the question and not of what happened to arrive".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the findings are worth keeping: "Partial findings stay in the claims, flagged, so a reader can use them and can see that they are incomplete."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system in which a coordinator delegates to specialised subagents. A run ends with three of four scopes covered, one unresolved error and one conflict between two sources. Which status does the report carry?

options.a: Complete, since a conflict is information and the scopes were mostly covered anyway
options.b: Partial, since one topic is missing, and the disagreement is listed beside it
options.c: Complete, since the unresolved error was only a timeout and nothing was lost
options.d: Failed, because an unresolved error invalidates the whole report

explanation.b: A missing scope makes the run partial, and a conflict is reported next to it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because completeness is about coverage: "A run is complete when every scope is covered."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the reason for a gap does not matter: "It is partial otherwise, whatever the reason, and the report says which scopes are missing and why."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the report is still useful: "A report that did not cover film is still a useful report".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system in which a coordinator delegates to specialised subagents. The synthesis agent's verification tool is asked to confirm a market-share figure that it cannot check locally. What should it return?

options.a: A verdict that a lookup is needed, which the hub routes onward
options.b: A confirmation, since the tool must leave no claim unchecked
options.c: An error that ends the synthesis step for the whole run
options.d: A guess at the figure based on the other claims in the report

explanation.a: Anything the tool cannot check goes back to be delegated.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the tool does not guess: "In the example, the tool answers for a date it can check, and returns `needs_search` for anything else."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a deep check stays where it was: "leaves the deep verification where it was: with the coordinator".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the tool exists to remove the round trip for the common case: "A scoped tool of this kind removes the round trip for the common case".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system in which a coordinator delegates to specialised subagents. A report's note lists `music (not researched)` beside `film (timeout on a query)`. What does the note tell the reader about music?

options.a: No subtask of the plan named it, so the fault is in the decomposition
options.b: Its search failed on a fault of the tool, with the query recorded
options.c: A source was searched and had nothing to say about it
options.d: A conflict between two sources left the topic incomplete

explanation.a: A scope that no result names was never planned: "A scope that no result names was never researched, which is the decomposition fault of page 1 and is fixed in the plan."
explanation.b: Ruled out because that is the phrasing for a failed search: "A scope whose search failed names the type and the query."
explanation.c: Ruled out because that is the third phrasing: "A scope with a result but no findings has no findings."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a conflict is not a gap: "A conflict does not change the status, because it is information the reader needs and not a missing piece."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system in which a coordinator delegates to specialised subagents. A claim rests on two findings: one that arrived before a subagent failed and one from a subagent that finished. Both agree. How is the claim flagged?

options.a: As incomplete, because one of its findings arrived from a run that failed
options.b: As conflicting, since the two findings came from two different runs
options.c: Without the incomplete mark, because a completed run backs it as well
options.d: As missing, because partial evidence cannot support a claim

explanation.c: One finished source is enough to remove the flag.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the flag needs every finding to be partial: "A claim is marked partial only when every finding behind it was partial".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the findings agree: "A conflict is two different values for one claim, not two sources for the same value".
explanation.d: Ruled out because partial findings stay as claims: "Partial findings stay in the claims, flagged, so a reader can use them and can see that they are incomplete."
